meta.title: Select the Deployment Model for the Insight Service
meta.subtitle: A decision brief comparing operational simplicity, isolation, delivery speed, and long-term cost.
meta.author: Platform Architecture

executive.answer: Adopt the managed container platform for the first production phase, with an explicit portability boundary around storage, messaging, and deployment manifests.
executive.scope: The decision covers the first two production regions and the next 18 months. It does not decide the analytics warehouse or end-user identity provider.
implications: The team accepts higher platform fees in exchange for faster delivery and lower operational burden.
Portability controls must be implemented before traffic and data volume make migration expensive.
executive.next_action: Approve the managed-platform option and assign the portability checklist before implementation begins.

metrics.label: Estimated path to the first production release
Current platform and service delivery team

items.title: Capacity constraint
items.summary: The current team cannot safely operate a new control plane and deliver the product workload on the same schedule.

items.title: Portability is required
items.summary: The service may move later, so data interfaces and deployment contracts cannot depend on proprietary runtime behavior.
details: Use standard container images and health checks.
Keep state in separately managed services with export paths.
Store deployment intent in version-controlled manifests.

items.title: Schedule pressure
items.summary: The first production release is committed for the current planning cycle.

sections.title: Options against shared criteria
sections.note: A comparison table is used instead of equal-height prose cards.

criteria.label: Delivery speed
criteria.description: Ability to meet the committed first-release date.

criteria.label: Operational burden
criteria.description: Control-plane ownership, upgrades, on-call scope, and recovery work.

criteria.label: Isolation
criteria.description: Ability to enforce workload and tenant boundaries.

criteria.label: Portability
criteria.description: Cost and complexity of moving the workload later.

criteria.label: 18-month cost
criteria.description: Platform fees plus credible engineering and operations effort.

items.title: Managed container platform
items.summary: Fastest credible route with the smallest new on-call surface.

values.cost: Higher platform fees, lower staffing burden

items.title: Self-managed orchestration
items.summary: Maximum infrastructure control, but it adds control-plane ownership immediately.

values.cost: Lower fees, materially higher engineering effort

items.title: Function-first serverless
items.summary: Low operational overhead for simple workloads, but the service has long-running and stateful processing paths.

values.cost: Efficient at low load; uncertain for sustained processing

items.title: Schedule risk dominates the first phase
items.summary: A self-managed control plane makes the product date depend on a second infrastructure project.
details: Consequence: delayed customer validation and a larger initial failure surface.
Action: choose a platform that already provides upgrades, control-plane availability, and baseline observability.

items.title: Lock-in is a design-control problem, not a reason to own everything
items.summary: The largest migration risks are proprietary state, event semantics, identity coupling, and deployment assumptions.
details: Consequence: portability can still degrade on a managed runtime.
Action: enforce the portability checklist in architecture review and CI.

items.title: Approve the managed container platform
items.summary: Record the choice, scope, assumptions, and review date in the architecture decision record.

items.title: Implement the portability checklist
items.summary: Cover images, health contracts, state export, event formats, secrets, identity, and deployment manifests.

items.title: Schedule an architecture re-evaluation
items.summary: Revisit the choice when staffing, load, regional footprint, or regulatory requirements materially change.
